shifts.summary: The shift was overall moderate. Reasoning was reported as moderate with candidates feeling confident on statement‑based items. Quantitative section was the toughest, many reported time pressure and difficulty ranging up to hard. English was consistently easy, while GA varied between easy‑moderate and moderate‑difficult.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported no trouble in reasoning, level was fine, and statements were moderate. One report called reasoning easy, another easy to moderate.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GA covered current affairs from 2024‑2025 and scheme‑related topics. Some reports found it easy‑moderate, others moderate‑difficult.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant was described as difficult, hard and highly calculative. Time pressure was noted with 25 questions in 15 minutes.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was described as very simple and easy across reports.

observations: Quant faced time pressure with 25 questions in 15 minutes.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 24 October 2026 comprised three shifts. Shift 1 was reported as moderate overall, with unofficial good‑attempt figures ranging from 70 to 85. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was reported as moderate overall, while Shift 2 was reported as moderate to difficult. Shift 3 has not been analysed yet, so no difficulty rating is available for that shift.

faqs.q: How many good attempts were reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: For Shift 1, candidates reported good attempts in the range of 70 to 85 questions. For Shift 2, the reported range was 62 to 72 questions. These numbers are unofficial and should be treated as indicative only.

faqs.q: Which sections were identified as most challenging on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: In Shift 1, the Quantitative section was noted as the toughest, with time pressure and difficulty up to hard. In Shift 2, Quantitative Aptitude leaned towards difficult, and Reasoning and General Awareness were also seen as moderate to difficult.

faqs.q: How does SSC normalise scores across different shifts for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 24 October 2026?
